A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same manifold-regression ICL work and contain readable main text, equations, and complete appendices. The earlier proof roadmap and Appendices A–C can be matched to the later Appendices B–E; the new empirical figures and table are also readable.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical constructions, generalization bounds, and proofs, including in its appendices. Its references to empirical findings concern other work; no original experimental or data-analysis outcomes are reported.

after.justification: v2 reports original spherical-harmonic regression experiments, attention–kernel correlations, testing-MSE scaling results, and attention analysis of GPT-2 on five sentences in Sections 4–5 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The embedding, positional encoding, empirical-risk objective, and five-block construction implementing Gaussian Nadaraya–Watson regression are retained. The construction still uses ReLU attention followed by masked softmax attention. v1 Appendix C.1 and v2 Appendix E.1 contain the same construction; the new experimental configurations do not introduce a new proposed method.

E1.justification: v1 has no empirical dataset or task coverage. v2 adds regression tasks generated from combinations of ten spherical harmonics on S^2 and diagnostic analysis of pretrained GPT-2 on five authored English sentences. These introduce actual synthetic and language-data evaluation.

E2.justification: v2 newly evaluates Gaussian-kernel scores as a reference comparator for learned attention scores in Figures 1 and 5 and Table 1. v1 connects these quantities only theoretically. This is a diagnostic comparison, without a benchmark comparison against alternative trained regressors; GPT-2 serves as a case study.

E3.justification: v2 introduces experimental protocols absent from v1: spherical-harmonic task generation, 50,000 tasks in each training/testing set for the correlation study, Pearson-correlation and MSE evaluation, prompt-length/task-count sweeps, and sorted GPT-2 attention analysis. Appendix F specifies model configurations and 100-epoch Adam training. These are new protocols, not revisions of earlier experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds mechanistic checks comparing learned attention with Gaussian kernels, distributions of per-sample correlations, additional examples in Appendix F, and a GPT-2 case study. Figure 4 also investigates sensitivity to prompt length and training-task count. v1 contains no corresponding empirical analyses.

E5.justification: v2 first reports correlation means, standard deviations, and associated p-value statistics over 5,000 independent testing samples in Table 1. The scaling study reports 30 repetitions and displays mean curves with standard-deviation bands in Figure 4. v1's probabilistic theoretical bounds do not constitute empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All empirical results are new. Table 1 reports mean correlations of 0.86, 0.75, 0.69, and 0.67 for prompt lengths 4, 8, 16, and 32. Figure 4 reports decreasing testing MSE and fitted prompt-length slopes of -0.071, -0.080, and -0.103 for 400, 1,600, and 6,400 training tasks. GPT-2 attention curves and additional kernel-comparison examples are also added.

T1.justification: Lemma 1 replaces the manifold, uniform-sampling, and Hölder assumptions inherited from Assumptions 1–2 with a bounded domain, a supported sampling distribution, and a bounded target function. The kernel bandwidth is stated as h > 0 instead of 0 < h < 1. Theorem 1 makes logarithmic factors explicit, while the main assumptions, construction proof, and supporting derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction newly claim that learned query–prompt scores are highly correlated with a Gaussian kernel and present numerical validation as a contribution. The principal claims about exact kernel implementation, intrinsic-dimension dependence, and near-minimax regression rates remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets attention correlations and GPT-2 curve shapes as support for the existing kernel perspective. It also explains flattening with increasing task count and faster prompt-length decay through the balance between the two existing error terms. The limitations concerning fixed prompts, noisy data, broader function classes, and limited training tasks are essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds data-generation instructions, experimental embedding dimensions, layer and head counts, batch size 100, Adam learning rate 0.0005, 100 training epochs, activation choices, and the five sentences with truncation instructions. Its new reproducibility statement reports supplementary training/evaluation code; actual code availability cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds discussions and citations to Cheng et al., Geshkovski et al., Han et al., Lu and Yu, and Tai et al. It acknowledges earlier kernel-based ICL interpretations and specifies the exact construction and manifold generalization bound as distinguishing contributions. The existing comparisons with Kim et al. and Li et al. remain.

P1.justification: The main narrative is substantially reorganized: the kernel connection precedes the generalization theorem, related work becomes a separate section, and the entire proof roadmap moves from Section 5 to Appendix C. The abstract and introduction are revised, and reproducibility, language-model-use, and experimental-detail sections are added.

P2.justification: v2 introduces five numbered figures and Table 1 where v1 has none. These include attention/kernel comparisons, correlation histograms, language attention curves, and six-panel scaling plots with uncertainty bands; Appendix F adds twelve example panels. This substantially changes the visual presentation beyond ordinary text reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the retained theory more assessable through quantitative attention diagnostics, repeated-run scaling results, experimental details, and clearer positioning. The gain is limited by the evidence: experiments cover one spherical-harmonic family, Section 4's uniform-angle sampling differs from Theorem 1's uniform-manifold assumption, and five sorted GPT-2 attention curves provide only illustrative support for the validation claims.
